dict.string:
Local front door: Caddy on port 80, loopback only, routing by hostname to local web apps so their links need no port number. Today one route: http://link.localhost -> link-bridge on 127.0.0.1:5465 (the pages that turn a web link into an app link: /reveal selects a file in Finder, /obsidian opens a note, /vault-setup opens or creates a vault). the link-bridge README, "Dropping the port".
WHY A ROOT LAUNCHDAEMON: binding port 80 as a user is refused on macOS (EACCES, Verified 2026-10-16), so Caddy must start as root. It is deliberately NOT `sudo brew services start caddy`: that leaves root-owned files under the Homebrew prefix and later breaks non-root `brew upgrade` and `brew cleanup`. This plist runs the Homebrew caddy binary directly; the binary stays brew-managed, the service does not.
WHY LOOPBACK ONLY: Caddy listens on all interfaces by default. The Caddyfile's global `default_bind 127.0.0.1 ::1` restricts every listener to loopback, since /reveal and /vault-setup act on this Mac. After any change run `lsof -nP -iTCP:80 -sTCP:LISTEN` and expect only 127.0.0.1:80 and [::1]:80.
DEPENDS ON: /opt/homebrew/opt/caddy/bin/caddy (brew formula caddy; the opt path survives upgrades), /usr/local/etc/link-bridge-front-door/Caddyfile (root-owned 0644, copied by install.sh from admin-technical frontdoor/), link-bridge running on 5465 (brew services, the logged-in user), and /etc/hosts lines "127.0.0.1 link.localhost" and "::1 link.localhost" for Safari and CLI tools (Chrome resolves *.localhost itself). Those lines keep Fleet policy 49 passing because it checks the address, not the name.
OPS: `sudo launchctl print system/com.link-bridge.front-door`; restart with `sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/com.link-bridge.front-door` after editing the Caddyfile (validate first: `caddy validate --config /usr/local/etc/link-bridge-front-door/Caddyfile`). Log: /Library/Logs/link-bridge-front-door.log. Health: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://link.localhost/reveal` -> 200, and `link-bridge doctor`. Remove with frontdoor/uninstall.sh.
